pattern_id: Phantom-Valid After Crash (Torn Block Persistence vs. Executed State)
description: Many blockchain/consensus implementations persist block data and execution results in multiple phases. If the system crashes between phases, storage can contain a block that appears “known” but is not executable because its post-state is missing. If the protocol’s external API (e.g., consensus/engine interface) equates “known block” with “valid block”, it can return a definitive validity decision (`VALID`, “committed”, “finalized”, etc.) without re-executing or confirming the state exists. This produces a “phantom-valid” block: externally affirmed as valid while internally lacking the necessary execution state, breaking consensus interface semantics and potentially causing agreement/liveness faults.
trigger_condition: - A node crashes/restarts after persisting “block presence” artifacts (header/body/receipts/canonical pointers) but before durably committing the block’s post-execution state (trie/snapshot) and/or an “executed” marker.
